Closed as the bead asked: the trade-off is recorded in the code so it is answered rather than rediscovered. No shape change.

The bead called it 'net-neutral' and 'marked opinion', wanting a future contributor not to reopen 'why aren't these generic?' without seeing the trade-off. RevocationCache's docs now carry a 'Why the methods are suffixed rather than generic' section with the GAT alternative written out and two reasons against it.

The first is cost distribution: an associated-type dance is paid by every consumer backing the cache with Redis or SQL, who would write CacheKey plumbing before writing any cache, in exchange for elegance in a trait they implement once.

The second has become stronger since the bead was filed and is the decisive one: PKIX-cr8.4 added guarded inserts (put_crl_unless_rollback, put_ocsp_unless_staler) whose comparison logic differs per protocol -- CRLNumber monotonicity is not thisUpdate monotonicity. A generic get/put/invalidate cannot express those, so they would need suffixed methods regardless and the trait would end up mixed rather than uniform. The method count is now eight, which makes the refactor more work for less payoff than when the bead was written. Commit a829edc8.
